decision: D1 BLEND REPAIR (ruled): today's [36,72] averages two cane types. ERECT is the default (spec §10.1): clemson_hgic blackberry "Erect varieties should be planted 2 to 4 feet apart in the row and 10 feet between rows." -> in_row [24,48], rows [120,120]. The same page's semi-trailing sentence ('6 to 8 feet apart in the row, with rows 10 feet apart') waits on plant_habit (R4; not this promote). Corroborating: UC MG SLO 3-4 ft in-row, 8-10 ft rows; USU erect 5 ft. Trellis-post spacing excluded. Restatements: the two planting_method rows 'rows 8 to 10 feet apart' -> 'rows about 10 feet apart' (Clemson states 10 ft for both types); the per-type in-row clauses already match.

edits.new: Plant dormant bare-root canes so the roots are an inch or two deep, then cut the old cane back to a few inches. Plant in late winter or early spring in cold areas, or over winter where winters are mild. Space upright types about 2 to 4 feet apart, and the big arching or trailing types about 6 to 8 feet apart, in rows about 10 feet apart. Use a slightly raised, well-drained row in full sun, and put up the trellis before the canes grow.
edits.reason: PLA-10 R3: rows follow the authored row_spacing_inches [120,120] (Clemson, both cane types)

edits.new: Plant dormant bare-root canes, setting the crown so the roots sit 1 to 2 inches below the surface, then cut the old handle cane back to a few inches. Plant in late winter or early spring in the North, or from late fall through winter in mild regions. Space erect types about 2 to 4 feet apart, and the vigorous semi-erect and trailing types about 6 to 8 feet apart, in rows about 10 feet apart. Plant on a slightly raised, well-drained row in full sun and install the trellis before growth begins; only compact erect types can be grown without support.
